a(n-1) + 1, & \text{if } n > 12 \text{ and } a(n-1) + 1 \neq 12 \cdot k \text{ for any integer } k \\
12 \cdot k, & \text{if } n > 12 \text{ and } a(n-1) + 1 = 12 \cdot k
\end{cases}
$$

---

### **Explanation**

- For $ n \leq 12 $, the sequence is just the natural numbers.
- For $ n > 12 $, the sequence increments by 1 unless the next value would be a multiple of 12. In that case, it jumps to the next multiple of 12.
- The jump occurs at specific indices (e.g., 13, 15, 18, 22, etc.), which are determined by the triangular number pattern.

This recursive definition captures the behavior of the sequence accurately based on the observed pattern.
